title: Asado del domingo en San Telmo

dialogue.speaker: Martín
dialogue.spanish: Che, Flor, acá en la carnicería del mercado queda el último kilo de vacío para el asado.
dialogue.english: Hey, Flor, right here at the market butcher shop they have the last kilo of flank steak for the barbecue.

dialogue.speaker: Flor
dialogue.spanish: ¡Qué joya! Llevate también cuatro chorizos y una bolsa de carbón antes de que se acabe.
dialogue.english: What a gem! Grab four sausages and a bag of charcoal too before it sells out.

dialogue.speaker: Martín
dialogue.spanish: Dale, son doce mil mangos en total. ¿Ponemos mitad y mitad o pagás vos las bebidas?
dialogue.english: Sounds good, it's twelve thousand pesos total. Should we split it fifty-fifty or do you want to buy the drinks?

slang.actualMeaning: bucks / pesos (classic Argentine slang for money)
slang.example: Esta campera me salió veinte mil mangos.

dialogue.speaker: Flor
dialogue.spanish: Yo compro el vino tinto y el pan acá al lado. ¡Nos va a quedar re copado el almuerzo!
dialogue.english: I'll buy the red wine and bread right next door. Lunch is going to turn out super cool!

slang.example: El lugar nuevo en Palermo está re copado.

questions.question: What items do Martín and Flor buy at the butcher shop for Sunday's barbecue?
options: The last kilo of 'vacío' (flank steak), four sausages ('chorizos'), and charcoal
Two chickens, potatoes, and salad greens
Fish fillets, lemons, and white wine
Pork ribs and a dozen empanadas
questions.explanation: Martín spots 'el último kilo de vacío' and Flor tells him: 'Llevate también cuatro chorizos y una bolsa de carbón.'

questions.question: How much does the butcher shop order cost in total?
questions.explanation: Martín says: 'Dale, son doce mil mangos en total' (12,000 pesos total).

questions.question: How do they divide the expenses for the barbecue?
options: Martín pays for the meat/charcoal, and Flor buys the red wine and bread next door
Flor pays for everything with her credit card
They ask their friends to transfer money first
They decide to eat at a restaurant instead
questions.explanation: Flor says: 'Yo compro el vino tinto y el pan acá al lado.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: In Argentina, what do 'doce mil mangos' and 're copado' mean?
options: 'Mangos' = tropical fruit; 're copado' = way too crowded
'Mangos' = coins; 're copado' = burnt on the grill
questions.explanation: In Argentine Spanish, 'mangos' means pesos/bucks, and 're copado' means super cool or awesome!
